_note: The season stories (EVAL-4, game redesign, 19 Oct 2026). DEMO CONTENT written by the builder: not pre-tested, merit tiers set by the builder (P1 rates them), Hinglish a draft. The warehouse season is built in full; the newsroom and clinic seasons are stubs. Beat counts, tie structures and every threshold the rating uses are PENDING v17 (generate v17 fixes them). Consequences are keyed by the merit tier of the description the player put first, never by who carried it.

premise.en: Five episodes in a busy warehouse, from the hiring sprint to the season close.
premise.hinglish: Ek vyast warehouse mein paanch episodes, hiring sprint se season ke ant tak.

intro.en: You lead a team of eight at Kite Logistics, a made-up warehouse company near Pune. The season runs in five short episodes, about ten decisions each, with the same team throughout.
intro.hinglish: Aap Kite Logistics mein aath logon ki team lead karte hain, Pune ke paas ek kaalpanik warehouse company. Season paanch chhote episodes mein chalta hai, har ek mein lagbhag das decisions, poore samay wahi team.

intro.en: Each screen is one decision. What you decide shows up on the next screen.
intro.hinglish: Har screen ek decision hai. Aapka decision agli screen par dikhta hai.

intro.en: To put colleagues in order, tap them, first choice first. The last one fills itself in.
intro.hinglish: Colleagues ko order mein rakhne ke liye unhe tap kijiye, pehli pasand pehle. Aakhri apne aap bhar jaata hai.

intro.en: To share something out, tap a number for each colleague.
intro.hinglish: Kuch baantne ke liye har colleague ke liye ek number tap kijiye.

intro.en: Changed your mind? Use Back on the next screen.
intro.hinglish: Mann badal gaya? Agli screen par Back dabaiye.

body.en: You meet the team in person. Here is who was who on the team chat.
body.hinglish: Aap team se khud milte hain. Team chat par kaun kaun tha, yeh raha.

scene.en: Lotus Home wants a first plan for its big sale by Friday.
scene.hinglish: Lotus Home ko apni badi sale ka pehla plan Friday tak chahiye.

question.en: Who should draft the peak plan? Put them in order.
question.hinglish: Peak plan kaun likhega? Inhe order mein rakhiye.

text.en: Wrote the peak plans for two clients last year; both were signed off first time.
text.hinglish: Pichhle saal do clients ke peak plan likhe; dono pehli baar mein approve hue.

text.en: Drafted last year's year-end plan; the client approved it without changes.
text.hinglish: Pichhle saal ka year-end plan likha; client ne bina badlaav approve kiya.

text.en: Has reviewed plans for others; not yet written one alone.
text.hinglish: Doosron ke plans review kiye hain; akele abhi tak koi nahin likha.

text.en: New to client plans; strong on spreadsheets, still learning how plans are set out.
text.hinglish: Client plans mein naya; spreadsheet mein mazboot, plan ka format abhi seekhna baaki.

3.en: {name} sent the plan on Friday morning. Lotus Home signed it off with one small note.
3.hinglish: {name} ne Friday subah plan bheja. Lotus Home ne ek chhote note ke saath approve kiya.

1.en: {name} sent the plan on Friday evening. Lotus Home asked for a second draft.
1.hinglish: {name} ne Friday shaam plan bheja. Lotus Home ne doosra draft maanga.

scene.en: A truck company can talk for twenty minutes today.
scene.hinglish: Ek truck company aaj bees minute baat kar sakti hai.

question.en: Who should take the transport call?

text.en: Has booked trucks for three peak seasons; knows the contract terms well.
text.hinglish: Teen peak seasons ke liye truck book kiye; contract ki sharten achhi tarah pata.

text.en: Ran the transport side of last year's peak; good at agreeing slots quickly.
text.hinglish: Pichhle saal peak ka transport sambhala; slots jaldi tay karne mein achha.

2.en: {name} took the call. The truck company is holding extra trucks for sale week.
2.hinglish: {name} ne call li. Truck company sale week ke liye extra trucks rok kar rakh rahi hai.

scene.en: The team's first video call is on Thursday.
scene.hinglish: Team ki pehli video call Thursday ko hai.

question.en: Snacks for the first team call?
question.hinglish: Pehli team call ke liye snacks?

text.en: Send each person a small snack box
text.hinglish: Har vyakti ko ek chhota snack box bhejein

after.en: The snack boxes arrive on Thursday morning. Cameras stay on.
after.hinglish: Snack boxes Thursday subah pahunch gaye. Camera on rahe.

text.en: Skip snacks this time
text.hinglish: Is baar snacks chhod dein

after.en: The call runs without snacks. It ends on time.
after.hinglish: Call bina snacks ke chali. Samay par khatam hui.

text.en: Pay back anything people buy
text.hinglish: Jo bhi log khareedein, uska paisa lautayein

after.en: Twelve receipts arrive by Friday, and accounts asks about each one.
after.hinglish: Friday tak baarah receipts aa gayi, aur accounts har ek ke baare mein pooch raha hai.

scene.en: The scanner maker offers 6 training days on the new handheld scanners.
scene.hinglish: Scanner company naye handheld scanners par 6 training din de rahi hai.

question.en: Share the 6 training days.

text.en: Will set up the scanners on the packing line; the training fits that job.
text.hinglish: Packing line par scanners lagane ka kaam; training usi kaam ke liye.

text.en: Trains new pickers every month; will pass the training on.
text.hinglish: Har mahine naye pickers ko training; yeh training aage sikhayi jaayegi.

text.en: Works in the office and rarely uses scanners.
text.hinglish: Office mein kaam; scanners ka istemaal kam.

3.en: {name} took the most training days. The packing line scanners are ready.
3.hinglish: Sabse zyada training din {name} ko mile. Packing line ke scanners taiyaar hain.

1.en: {name} took the most training days. The packing line scanners still need setting up.
1.hinglish: Sabse zyada training din {name} ko mile. Packing line ke scanners abhi lagne baaki hain.

even.en: The training days were shared evenly. Three colleagues know the new scanners.
even.hinglish: Training din barabar baante gaye. Teen colleagues naye scanners jaante hain.

scene.en: Lotus Home wants someone to walk the warehouse floor with them.
scene.hinglish: Lotus Home chahta hai ki koi unke saath warehouse floor ghoome.

question.en: Who should lead the floor walk? Put them in order.
question.hinglish: Floor walk kaun lead karega? Inhe order mein rakhiye.

text.en: Led client floor walks for four peak seasons; spots bottlenecks early.
text.hinglish: Chaar peak seasons mein client floor walks lead kiye; rukawatein jaldi pakadne mein achha.

text.en: Planned the current shelf layout; knows how stock moves through the floor.
text.hinglish: Abhi ka shelf layout plan kiya; floor par stock kaise chalta hai, achhi tarah pata.

text.en: Has joined one floor walk as a note taker.
text.hinglish: Ek floor walk mein note taker ke roop mein shaamil.

text.en: Mostly works on the budget side; has not walked the floor with a client.
text.hinglish: Zyaadatar budget ka kaam; client ke saath floor walk nahin kiya.

3.en: {name} walked the floor with the client. They agreed where the sale stock goes.
3.hinglish: {name} ne client ke saath floor walk kiya. Sale stock ki jagah tay ho gayi.

1.en: {name} walked the floor with the client. Where the sale stock goes is still open.
1.hinglish: {name} ne client ke saath floor walk kiya. Sale stock ki jagah abhi tay nahin hui.

scene.en: Someone writes the weekly update for the client.
scene.hinglish: Client ke liye weekly update koi likhta hai.

question.en: Who should write this week's update?
question.hinglish: Is hafte ka update kaun likhega?

text.en: Writes the warehouse newsletter; clear, short and always on time.
text.hinglish: Warehouse newsletter likhne ka kaam; saaf, chhota aur hamesha samay par.

text.en: Prefers talking to writing; updates tend to run long.
text.hinglish: Likhne se zyada baat karna pasand; updates lambe ho jaate hain.

3.en: {name} sent the update. The client replied with a thumbs up.
3.hinglish: {name} ne update bheja. Client ne thumbs up bheja.

1.en: {name} sent the update. The client asked two questions about it.
1.hinglish: {name} ne update bheja. Client ne us par do sawaal poochhe.

scene.en: Forty temporary pickers apply in one week, and the interview panel needs a lead.
scene.hinglish: Ek hafte mein chaalis temporary pickers apply karte hain, aur interview panel ko ek lead chahiye.

question.en: Who should lead the interview panel? Put them in order.
question.hinglish: Interview panel kaun lead karega? Inhe order mein rakhiye.

text.en: Led the interview panel for the last two peaks; most hires stayed the whole season.
text.hinglish: Pichhle do peaks mein interview panel lead kiya; zyaadatar log poore season ruke.

text.en: Trained as an interviewer last year and runs the warehouse's skills tests.
text.hinglish: Pichhle saal interviewer ki training li; warehouse ke skills tests chalane ka kaam.

text.en: Has sat on one panel as an observer.
text.hinglish: Ek panel mein observer ke roop mein baithe hain.

text.en: Has not interviewed anyone for the warehouse.
text.hinglish: Warehouse ke liye kisi ka interview nahin liya.

3.en: {name} led the panel. Thirty-eight of the forty start on Monday.
3.hinglish: {name} ne panel lead kiya. Chaalis mein se adtees Monday se shuru karenge.

1.en: {name} led the panel. The interviews run two days over.
1.hinglish: {name} ne panel lead kiya. Interviews do din zyada chale.

scene.en: Sale week needs 40 temporary pickers, trained and on a rota.
scene.hinglish: Sale week ke liye 40 temporary pickers chahiye, training aur rota ke saath.

question.en: Who should run the temp staff plan? Put them in order.
question.hinglish: Temp staff plan kaun chalayega? Inhe order mein rakhiye.

text.en: Recruited 30 temporary staff last peak and set up the rota; nobody missed a shift.
text.hinglish: Pichhle peak mein 30 temporary staff rakhe aur rota banaya; kisi ki shift nahin chhooti.

text.en: Runs the warehouse's training programme; has trained 200 new pickers.
text.hinglish: Warehouse ka training programme chalane ka kaam; 200 naye pickers ko training di.

text.en: Has helped on the induction desk once.
text.hinglish: Ek baar induction desk par madad ki.

text.en: Good with schedules in general; has not worked with temporary staff.
text.hinglish: Schedules mein aam taur par achha; temporary staff ke saath kaam nahin kiya.

3.en: {name} opened the temp rota. 25 pickers signed up on the first day.
3.hinglish: {name} ne temp rota khola. Pehle din 25 pickers jude.

1.en: {name} opened the temp rota. 8 pickers signed up on the first day.
1.hinglish: {name} ne temp rota khola. Pehle din 8 pickers jude.

scene.en: A staffing agency could supply temporary pickers.
scene.hinglish: Ek staffing agency temporary pickers de sakti hai.

question.en: Who should write to the agency?

text.en: Hired temporary staff for the last two peaks; knows the agency's team.
text.hinglish: Pichhle do peaks mein temporary staff rakha; agency ki team ko jaante hain.

text.en: Has not worked with a staffing agency before.
text.hinglish: Staffing agency ke saath pehle kaam nahin kiya.

3.en: {name} wrote to the agency. They can send 40 pickers.
3.hinglish: {name} ne agency ko likha. Woh 40 pickers bhej sakte hain.

1.en: {name} wrote to the agency. No reply yet.
1.hinglish: {name} ne agency ko likha. Abhi tak jawab nahin aaya.

scene.en: The client asks for a stock count on a Saturday.
scene.hinglish: Client Saturday ko stock count chahta hai.

question.en: What about the Saturday count?

text.en: Hold it, and give the team a day off in lieu
text.hinglish: Count karein, aur team ko badle mein ek din ki chhutti dein

after.en: The Saturday count goes ahead. Monday is a quiet day off.
after.hinglish: Saturday count ho gaya. Monday aaraam ki chhutti hai.

text.en: Move it to a weekday evening
text.hinglish: Ise kisi weekday ki shaam par le jaayein

after.en: The count moves to Wednesday evening. Two people join late.
after.hinglish: Count Wednesday shaam ko hua. Do log der se jude.

text.en: Hold it with no day off
text.hinglish: Count karein, koi chhutti nahin

after.en: The count goes ahead. The team is tired on Monday.
after.hinglish: Count ho gaya. Monday ko team thaki hui hai.

scene.en: Two complaints reach you on Monday, each saying a colleague took credit for their work.
scene.hinglish: Monday ko do shikayatein aati hain, dono mein kaha gaya ki kisi colleague ne unke kaam ka credit le liya.

question.en: Whose complaint do you take up first?
question.hinglish: Aap pehle kiski shikayat uthaate hain?

text.en: Says the new shift rota was presented as someone else's work; has the dated draft.
text.hinglish: Kehte hain ki naya shift rota kisi aur ke kaam ke roop mein dikhaya gaya; date wala draft hai.

text.en: Says the returns fix was claimed by someone else on the client call; has the emails.
text.hinglish: Kehte hain ki client call par returns fix ka credit kisi aur ne liya; emails hain.

2.en: You start with {name}'s complaint. Both complaints are looked into by the end of the week.
2.hinglish: Aap {name} ki shikayat se shuru karte hain. Hafte ke aakhir tak dono shikayaton ki jaanch ho jaati hai.

scene.en: There was a shouting match on the loading dock. Four colleagues give you their account.
scene.hinglish: Loading dock par zor ki bahas hui. Chaar colleagues apna bayaan dete hain.

question.en: Whose account do you rely on most? Put them in order.
question.hinglish: Aap kiske bayaan par sabse zyada bharosa karenge? Inhe order mein rakhiye.

text.en: Was on the dock throughout and wrote down what happened the same hour.
text.hinglish: Poore samay dock par the aur usi ghante likh liya ki kya hua.

text.en: Was loading the next truck, saw all of it, and gave the same account twice.
text.hinglish: Agla truck load kar rahe the, sab dekha, aur do baar ek jaisa bayaan diya.

text.en: Arrived at the end and heard the rest from others.
text.hinglish: Aakhir mein pahunche aur baaki doosron se suna.

text.en: Was on a break and heard it from the canteen.
text.hinglish: Break par the aur canteen se suna.

3.en: {name}'s account holds up against the shift logs. The matter is settled by Friday.
3.hinglish: {name} ka bayaan shift logs se mel khaata hai. Friday tak maamla suljh gaya.

1.en: {name}'s account has gaps the shift logs do not fill. The matter drags into next week.
1.hinglish: {name} ke bayaan mein kamiyan hain jo shift logs se nahin bhartin. Maamla agle hafte tak khinch gaya.

scene.en: Two colleagues raise the same concern: overtime hours were left off their pay slips.
scene.hinglish: Do colleagues ek hi chinta uthaate hain: overtime ke ghante pay slip mein nahin jude.

question.en: Whose concern goes to payroll first?
question.hinglish: Kiski chinta pehle payroll ko jaayegi?

text.en: Kept a daily log of hours that matches the gate records.
text.hinglish: Ghanton ka roz ka log rakha jo gate records se milta hai.

text.en: Has the shift lead's signed overtime sheet for each day.
text.hinglish: Har din ki shift lead ki sign ki hui overtime sheet hai.

2.en: {name}'s concern goes first. Payroll fixes both pay slips this month.
2.hinglish: {name} ki chinta pehle gayi. Payroll ne is mahine dono pay slips theek kar di.

scene.en: The team asks how concerns should be raised from now on.
scene.hinglish: Team poochhti hai ki ab se chintaayein kaise uthaayi jaayein.

question.en: How should concerns be raised?

text.en: A simple form, with a reply within a week
text.hinglish: Ek seedha form, ek hafte mein jawab ke saath

after.en: The form goes up on the notice board.
after.hinglish: Form notice board par lag gaya.

text.en: Come and see me any time
text.hinglish: Kabhi bhi mujhse mil lijiye

after.en: Two people come by. Others say they are not sure it is welcome.
after.hinglish: Do log aaye. Baaki kehte hain unhe pakka nahin ki yeh theek rahega.

text.en: Raise it at the weekly meeting, in front of everyone
text.hinglish: Weekly meeting mein sabke saamne uthaiye

after.en: Nobody raises anything at the weekly meeting.
after.hinglish: Weekly meeting mein koi kuch nahin uthaata.

scene.en: Two colleagues each ask for a quiet word: they are often spoken over in shift meetings.
scene.hinglish: Do colleagues alag alag baat karna chahte hain: shift meetings mein unki baat aksar kaati jaati hai.

question.en: You have time for one this week. Who do you meet first?
question.hinglish: Is hafte ek ke liye samay hai. Pehle kisse milenge?

text.en: Gives three recent examples, with the meeting dates.
text.hinglish: Haal ke teen udaharan dete hain, meeting ki tareekhon ke saath.

text.en: Gives three recent examples, and a colleague confirms each one.
text.hinglish: Haal ke teen udaharan dete hain, aur ek colleague unki pushti karta hai.

2.en: You meet {name} first. Shift meetings get a round where everyone speaks once.
2.hinglish: Aap pehle {name} se milte hain. Shift meetings mein ab har koi ek baar bolta hai.

scene.en: Two colleagues disagree about how the stock miscount happened.
scene.hinglish: Do colleagues mein behas hai ki stock ki ginti galat kaise hui.

question.en: Whose account goes in the incident report?
question.hinglish: Incident report mein kiska bayaan jaayega?

text.en: Matches the scanner records line by line.
text.hinglish: Scanner records se line dar line milta hai.

text.en: Remembers it differently from the scanner records.
text.hinglish: Scanner records se alag yaad hai.

3.en: {name}'s account goes in. The scanner check is added to the count routine.
3.hinglish: {name} ka bayaan gaya. Ginti ke tareeke mein scanner check jod diya gaya.

1.en: {name}'s account goes in. Audit asks why it differs from the scanner records.
1.hinglish: {name} ka bayaan gaya. Audit poochhta hai ki yeh scanner records se alag kyon hai.

scene.en: Four colleagues report safety concerns. The safety meeting can take two this week.
scene.hinglish: Chaar colleagues safety chintaayein batate hain. Is hafte safety meeting do le sakti hai.

question.en: Whose concern goes to the safety meeting first? Put them in order.
question.hinglish: Kiski chinta pehle safety meeting mein jaayegi? Inhe order mein rakhiye.

text.en: Photographed a cracked rack upright and logged the bay number.
text.hinglish: Toote rack ka photo liya aur bay number likha.

text.en: Measured a blocked fire exit route and logged it twice this month.
text.hinglish: Band fire exit raaste ko naapa aur is mahine do baar log kiya.

text.en: Mentions that the floor felt slippery somewhere last week.
text.hinglish: Kehte hain ki pichhle hafte kahin farsh fisalne wala laga.

text.en: Heard from someone that a forklift beeps oddly.
text.hinglish: Kisi se suna ki ek forklift ajeeb aawaaz karta hai.

3.en: {name}'s concern goes first. The repair is booked for Tuesday.
3.hinglish: {name} ki chinta pehle gayi. Marammat Tuesday ko book hui.

1.en: {name}'s concern goes first. The meeting asks for more detail before acting.
1.hinglish: {name} ki chinta pehle gayi. Meeting ne kaam se pehle aur jaankari maangi.

scene.en: A customer complains about a damaged parcel. Two colleagues packed orders at that table.
scene.hinglish: Ek customer toote parcel ki shikayat karta hai. Us table par do colleagues ne orders pack kiye.

question.en: Whose packing record do you send to the customer team?
question.hinglish: Kiska packing record customer team ko bhejenge?

text.en: Packed by the standard and photographed every parcel that morning.
text.hinglish: Standard ke hisaab se pack kiya aur us subah har parcel ka photo liya.

text.en: Packed by the standard and has the checker's sign-off for every parcel.
text.hinglish: Standard ke hisaab se pack kiya aur har parcel par checker ka sign-off hai.

2.en: {name}'s record goes to the customer team. The parcel was damaged in transit.
2.hinglish: {name} ka record customer team ko gaya. Parcel raaste mein toota tha.

scene.en: Four colleagues say the holiday rota went against them last year.
scene.hinglish: Chaar colleagues kehte hain ki pichhle saal holiday rota unke khilaaf gaya.

question.en: Whose case do you look at first? Put them in order.
question.hinglish: Aap pehle kiska maamla dekhenge? Inhe order mein rakhiye.

text.en: Worked every public holiday last year, by the rota records.
text.hinglish: Rota records ke hisaab se pichhle saal har public holiday par kaam kiya.

text.en: Was given no leave in either peak, by the rota records.
text.hinglish: Rota records ke hisaab se dono peaks mein koi chhutti nahin mili.

text.en: Had one holiday swapped, by agreement.
text.hinglish: Sehmati se ek chhutti badli gayi.

text.en: Had the leave asked for, by the rota records.
text.hinglish: Rota records ke hisaab se maangi gayi chhutti mili.

3.en: You look at {name}'s case first. The new rota spreads holidays more evenly.
3.hinglish: Aap pehle {name} ka maamla dekhte hain. Naya rota chhuttiyaan zyada barabar baant ta hai.

1.en: You look at {name}'s case first. Two others ask why theirs waited.
1.hinglish: Aap pehle {name} ka maamla dekhte hain. Do aur poochhte hain ki unka maamla kyon ruka.

scene.en: The disputes have taken a week. The team is tense.
scene.hinglish: Jhagdon mein ek hafta laga. Team mein tanaav hai.

question.en: How do you close the week?

text.en: A short team meeting on what changes now
text.hinglish: Ab kya badlega, us par chhoti team meeting

after.en: The meeting is short. People leave knowing what changes.
after.hinglish: Meeting chhoti rahi. Log jaante hain ki kya badlega.

text.en: An email to everyone
text.hinglish: Sabko ek email

after.en: The email goes out. A few people reply.
after.hinglish: Email chala gaya. Kuch logon ne jawab diya.

text.en: Say nothing and move on
text.hinglish: Kuch na kahein aur aage badhein

after.en: Nobody is sure the matter is closed.
after.hinglish: Kisi ko pakka nahin ki maamla khatam hua.

scene.en: The peak budget needs one owner.
scene.hinglish: Peak budget ka ek owner chahiye.

question.en: Who should own the budget sheet?

text.en: Kept last year's peak budget within one per cent of plan.
text.hinglish: Pichhle saal ka peak budget plan ke ek pratishat ke andar rakha.

text.en: Runs the warehouse's monthly cost reports; spots overspends early.
text.hinglish: Warehouse ki monthly cost reports ka kaam; zyada kharch jaldi pakadne mein achha.

2.en: {name} owns the budget sheet now. The first version is shared with the client.
2.hinglish: Budget sheet ab {name} ke paas hai. Pehla version client ko bheja gaya.

scene.en: Sale week needs thousands of packing boxes.
scene.hinglish: Sale week ke liye hazaaron packing boxes chahiye.

question.en: Which box supplier?

text.en: The local supplier the warehouse has used before
text.hinglish: Local supplier jiske saath warehouse pehle kaam kar chuka hai

after.en: The local supplier delivers samples in two days.
after.hinglish: Local supplier ne do din mein samples bhej diye.

text.en: The cheapest supplier online
text.hinglish: Online sabse sasta supplier

after.en: The online samples arrive a week late, and a little thin.
after.hinglish: Online samples ek hafte der se aaye, aur thode patle.

text.en: Let each shift order its own
text.hinglish: Har shift apne boxes khud mangaye

after.en: Five suppliers send five different box sizes.
after.hinglish: Paanch suppliers ne paanch alag size ke boxes bheje.

scene.en: A forklift safety course runs over 6 days, and the days can be split between colleagues.
scene.hinglish: Forklift safety course 6 din ka hai, aur din colleagues mein baante ja sakte hain.

question.en: Share the 6 course days.

text.en: Already runs the forklift checks; the course would make it official.
text.hinglish: Forklift checks pehle se sambhalne ka kaam; course se yeh official hoga.

text.en: Will lead the loading dock in sale week; the course covers exactly that.
text.hinglish: Sale week mein loading dock lead karne ka kaam; course bilkul usi ke baare mein.

text.en: Interested in safety work; no safety role in sale week.
text.hinglish: Safety ke kaam mein dilchaspi; sale week mein koi safety role nahin.

3.en: {name} took the most course days and is now writing the sale week safety plan.
3.hinglish: Sabse zyada course din {name} ko mile, aur ab sale week ka safety plan unke haath mein hai.

1.en: {name} took the most course days. The safety plan still needs a lead.
1.hinglish: Sabse zyada course din {name} ko mile. Safety plan ko abhi bhi ek lead chahiye.

even.en: The course days were shared evenly. Three colleagues know the safety basics.
even.hinglish: Course din barabar baante gaye. Teen colleagues safety ki buniyadi baatein jaante hain.

scene.en: Twelve suppliers need peak contracts this week.
scene.hinglish: Is hafte baarah suppliers ke peak contracts karne hain.

question.en: Who should lead the supplier deals? Put them in order.
question.hinglish: Supplier deals kaun lead karega? Inhe order mein rakhiye.

text.en: Negotiated last peak's supplier contracts and saved 15 per cent.
text.hinglish: Pichhle peak ke supplier contracts tay kiye aur 15 pratishat bachaya.

text.en: Manages the warehouse's supplier list; has worked with eight of the twelve.
text.hinglish: Warehouse ki supplier list sambhalne ka kaam; baarah mein se aath ke saath kaam kiya.

text.en: Has sat in on two supplier meetings.
text.hinglish: Do supplier meetings mein baithe hain.

text.en: Strong on paperwork; has not negotiated a contract.
text.hinglish: Kaagzi kaam mein mazboot; koi contract tay nahin kiya.

3.en: {name} closed eleven of the twelve deals under budget.
3.hinglish: {name} ne baarah mein se gyaarah deals budget ke andar poori ki.

1.en: {name} closed seven deals. Five are still open.
1.hinglish: {name} ne saat deals poori ki. Paanch abhi baaki hain.

scene.en: The forecast shows heavy rain in sale week.
scene.hinglish: Forecast ke hisaab se sale week mein tez baarish hogi.

question.en: What about the loading dock?

text.en: Book covers for the loading dock now
text.hinglish: Loading dock ke liye abhi covers book karein

after.en: The dock covers are booked.
after.hinglish: Dock covers book ho gaye.

text.en: Wait for a closer forecast
text.hinglish: Paas ke forecast ka intezaar karein

after.en: The forecast still says rain. Covers cost more now.
after.hinglish: Forecast ab bhi baarish bata raha hai. Covers ab mehenge hain.

text.en: Load the trucks in the rain
text.hinglish: Baarish mein hi trucks load karein

after.en: The client is not happy about wet boxes.
after.hinglish: Geele boxes se client khush nahin hai.

scene.en: Someone has to take minutes at 6 client meetings. It is useful, but nobody asks for it.
scene.hinglish: 6 client meetings ke minutes kisi ko likhne hain. Kaam zaroori hai, par koi ise maangta nahin.

question.en: Share the 6 sets of minutes.

text.en: Has the lightest workload this month.
text.hinglish: Is mahine sabse halka kaam.

text.en: Has a light month after finishing the budget work early.
text.hinglish: Budget ka kaam jaldi khatam hone ke baad is mahine kaam halka.

text.en: Is carrying two other deadlines this month.
text.hinglish: Is mahine do aur deadlines saath mein.

3.en: {name} took the most minutes. The notes go out the same day.
3.hinglish: Sabse zyada minutes {name} ke paas gaye. Notes usi din nikal gaye.

1.en: {name} took the most minutes on top of two deadlines. The notes go out late.
1.hinglish: Do deadlines ke saath sabse zyada minutes {name} ke paas gaye. Notes der se nikle.

even.en: The minutes were shared evenly. The notes go out within two days.
even.hinglish: Minutes barabar baante gaye. Notes do din ke andar nikal gaye.

scene.en: The truck company has pulled out, ten days before the sale.
scene.hinglish: Sale se das din pehle truck company peeche hat gayi.

question.en: Who should handle the truck crisis? Put them in order.
question.hinglish: Truck crisis kaun sambhalega? Inhe order mein rakhiye.

text.en: Found replacement trucks at two days' notice during last year's peak.
text.hinglish: Pichhle peak mein do din ke notice par doosre trucks dhoondhe.

text.en: Has contacts at three truck firms; handled a cancelled booking last month.
text.hinglish: Teen truck firms mein jaan-pehchaan; pichhle mahine ek cancel booking sambhali.

text.en: Calm under pressure; has not dealt with a supplier problem.
text.hinglish: Dabaav mein shaant; supplier ki kisi samasya se nahin nipte.

text.en: Joined the transport team recently; still learning who to call.
text.hinglish: Transport team mein haal hi mein shaamil; kise call karna hai, abhi seekhna baaki.

3.en: {name} found a new truck firm by Friday, at the same price.
3.hinglish: {name} ne Friday tak nayi truck firm dhoondh li, usi daam par.

1.en: {name} found a new truck firm, at a higher price.
1.hinglish: {name} ne nayi truck firm dhoondh li, zyada daam par.

scene.en: The team is behind on labelling the new shelves.
scene.hinglish: Team naye shelves par label lagane mein peeche hai.

question.en: How do you catch up?

text.en: Hire two temporary helpers for a week
text.hinglish: Ek hafte ke liye do temporary helpers rakhein

after.en: The helpers start on Tuesday. The labels catch up.
after.hinglish: Helpers Tuesday se aaye. Labels ka kaam poora hone laga.

text.en: Ask for voluntary overtime
text.hinglish: Apni marzi se overtime ke liye poochhein

after.en: Three people stay late twice. The labels are nearly done.
after.hinglish: Teen log do baar der tak ruke. Labels lagbhag ho gaye.

text.en: Skip the shelf labels
text.hinglish: Shelf labels chhod dein

after.en: Pickers ask where the shelf labels went.
after.hinglish: Pickers pooch rahe hain ki shelf labels kahan gaye.

scene.en: Sale week brings returns too.
scene.hinglish: Sale week mein returns bhi aate hain.

question.en: Who should set up the returns desk?

text.en: Ran last peak's returns desk; it handled 3,000 returns without a backlog.
text.hinglish: Pichhle peak ka returns desk chalaya; 3,000 returns bina rukawat ke sambhale.

text.en: Has not worked on returns before.
text.hinglish: Returns par pehle kaam nahin kiya.

3.en: {name} set up the returns desk. A test run takes ten seconds a parcel.
3.hinglish: {name} ne returns desk lagaya. Test run mein ek parcel par das second lage.

1.en: {name} set up the returns desk. The test run is slow.
1.hinglish: {name} ne returns desk lagaya. Test run dheema hai.

scene.en: The new conveyor belt arrives on Thursday.
scene.hinglish: Naya conveyor belt Thursday ko aa raha hai.

question.en: Who should run the conveyor test?

text.en: Has tested the last six machines the warehouse bought.
text.hinglish: Warehouse ki pichhli chhah machines ka test kiya.

text.en: Has never tested a machine.
text.hinglish: Kabhi kisi machine ka test nahin kiya.

3.en: {name} ran the test. The belt runs first time.
3.hinglish: {name} ne test kiya. Belt pehli baar mein chal gaya.

1.en: {name} ran the test. One motor has to be replaced.
1.hinglish: {name} ne test kiya. Ek motor badalni padegi.

scene.en: Lotus Home's directors want to hear the plan in person.
scene.hinglish: Lotus Home ke directors plan khud sunna chahte hain.

question.en: Who should present the plan? Put them in order.
question.hinglish: Plan kaun present karega? Inhe order mein rakhiye.

text.en: Presented to the company's two biggest clients this year; both renewed.
text.hinglish: Is saal company ke do sabse bade clients ko present kiya; dono ne contract badhaya.

text.en: Pitched last year's peak plan to a new client and won the contract.
text.hinglish: Pichhle saal naye client ko peak plan pitch kiya aur contract jeeta.

text.en: Has presented inside the team; not yet to a client's directors.
text.hinglish: Team ke andar present kiya hai; client ke directors ko abhi tak nahin.

text.en: Knows the plan's numbers best; nervous in front of large groups.
text.hinglish: Plan ke numbers sabse achhe se pata; bade group ke saamne ghabrahat.

3.en: {name} presented the plan. The directors approved the budget in the room.
3.hinglish: {name} ne plan present kiya. Directors ne wahin budget approve kiya.

1.en: {name} presented the plan. The directors want to see it again next week.
1.hinglish: {name} ne plan present kiya. Directors agle hafte phir dekhna chahte hain.

scene.en: The client wants a packing standard for fragile goods.
scene.hinglish: Client ko naazuk saamaan ke liye packing standard chahiye.

question.en: Who should write the packing standard?

text.en: Wrote the packing standards for two glassware clients; breakages fell.
text.hinglish: Do glassware clients ke packing standard likhe; toot-phoot kam hui.

text.en: Trains the packing line; has a sharp eye for damage.
text.hinglish: Packing line ko training; nuksan pakadne ki tez nazar.

2.en: {name} wrote the packing standard. The client adds it to the contract.
2.hinglish: {name} ne packing standard likha. Client ne use contract mein jod diya.

scene.en: The sale stock needs 60 new shelf bays.
scene.hinglish: Sale stock ke liye 60 naye shelf bays chahiye.

question.en: Who should plan the shelf layout?

text.en: Planned last year's 50 sale bays; pickers found every item.
text.hinglish: Pichhle saal ke 50 sale bays plan kiye; pickers ko har item mil gaya.

text.en: Trained in space planning; laid out the returns area last year.
text.hinglish: Space planning mein trained; pichhle saal returns area ka layout banaya.

2.en: {name} planned the shelves. Every bay fits, with room for a returns lane.
2.hinglish: {name} ne shelves plan kiye. Har bay fit hai, returns lane ki jagah bhi hai.

scene.en: Twenty small sellers can ship through the warehouse in sale week.
scene.hinglish: Sale week mein bees chhote sellers warehouse se maal bhej sakte hain.

question.en: Who should get in touch with the sellers?

text.en: Speaks with small sellers every month for the warehouse's marketplace line.
text.hinglish: Warehouse ki marketplace line ke liye har mahine chhote sellers se baat.

text.en: Set up last year's small seller desk; many sellers know the name.
text.hinglish: Pichhle saal small seller desk shuru kiya; kai sellers naam se jaante hain.

2.en: {name} called the sellers. Eighteen of twenty have signed up.
2.hinglish: {name} ne sellers ko call kiya. Bees mein se atharah jud gaye.

scene.en: Lotus Home's auditors will inspect the warehouse.
scene.hinglish: Lotus Home ke auditors warehouse ki jaanch karenge.

question.en: Who should host the audit? Put them in order.
question.hinglish: Audit kaun host karega? Inhe order mein rakhiye.

text.en: Hosted last year's client audit; it passed with no findings.
text.hinglish: Pichhle saal ka client audit host kiya; bina kisi kami ke paas hua.

text.en: Former quality inspector; knows what auditors look for.
text.hinglish: Pehle quality inspector; auditors kya dekhte hain, achhi tarah pata.

text.en: Has prepared audit files; has not met auditors in person.
text.hinglish: Audit files taiyaar ki hain; auditors se kabhi mile nahin.

text.en: Prefers working behind the scenes; has not done audit work.
text.hinglish: Parde ke peeche kaam pasand; audit ka kaam nahin kiya.

3.en: {name} hosted the audit. It passed with no findings.
3.hinglish: {name} ne audit host kiya. Bina kisi kami ke paas hua.

1.en: {name} hosted the audit. It passed with three small findings.
1.hinglish: {name} ne audit host kiya. Teen chhoti kamiyon ke saath paas hua.

scene.en: The client's directors want a walkthrough of the plan.
scene.hinglish: Client ke directors plan ka walkthrough chahte hain.

question.en: Who should take the directors through the plan?

text.en: Knows every part of the plan; explains numbers simply.
text.hinglish: Plan ka har hissa pata; numbers aasaani se samjhane mein achha.

text.en: Has walked this client through two earlier projects.
text.hinglish: Is client ko pehle do projects samjhaye hain.

2.en: {name} took the directors through the plan. They asked for a faster returns lane.
2.hinglish: {name} ne directors ko plan samjhaya. Unhone tez returns lane maangi.

scene.en: The company director offers 6 hours of one to one mentoring.
scene.hinglish: Company director 6 ghante ki one to one mentoring de rahe hain.

question.en: Share the 6 mentoring hours.

text.en: Is preparing to lead a site next year; the mentoring fits that plan.
text.hinglish: Agle saal ek site lead karne ki taiyaari; mentoring usi plan ke liye.

text.en: Has asked for help with client strategy, which the director knows well.
text.hinglish: Client strategy mein madad maangi hai, jo director achhi tarah jaante hain.

text.en: Has not asked for mentoring and is happy in the current role.
text.hinglish: Mentoring nahin maangi; abhi ke role mein khush.

3.en: {name} took the most mentoring hours and has a first session on Monday.
3.hinglish: Sabse zyada mentoring ghante {name} ko mile; pehla session Monday ko hai.

1.en: {name} took the most mentoring hours, with no questions ready yet.
1.hinglish: Sabse zyada mentoring ghante {name} ko mile, par sawaal abhi taiyaar nahin.

even.en: The mentoring hours were shared evenly. Three first sessions are booked.
even.hinglish: Mentoring ghante barabar baante gaye. Teen pehle sessions book hue.

scene.en: The floor needs signs in English, Hindi and Marathi.
scene.hinglish: Floor par English, Hindi aur Marathi mein signs chahiye.

question.en: Who should check the signs?

text.en: Edited the warehouse's Hindi and Marathi notices for two years.
text.hinglish: Do saal se warehouse ke Hindi aur Marathi notices edit kiye.

text.en: Translated last year's floor signs into three languages.
text.hinglish: Pichhle saal ke floor signs teen bhashaon mein translate kiye.

2.en: {name} checked the signs. Every sign reads correctly in all three languages.
2.hinglish: {name} ne signs check kiye. Har sign teeno bhashaon mein sahi hai.

scene.en: Sale week runs a night shift for the first time.
scene.hinglish: Sale week mein pehli baar night shift chalegi.

question.en: Who should lead the night shift? Put them in order.
question.hinglish: Night shift kaun lead karega? Inhe order mein rakhiye.

text.en: Led the night shift through two peaks at another warehouse.
text.hinglish: Doosre warehouse mein do peaks tak night shift lead ki.

text.en: Ran last peak's busiest shift; every truck left on time.
text.hinglish: Pichhle peak ki sabse vyast shift chalayi; har truck samay par nikla.

text.en: Has covered one night shift.
text.hinglish: Ek night shift cover ki hai.

text.en: Keen to lead; has not run a shift.
text.hinglish: Lead karne ka shauk; koi shift nahin chalayi.

3.en: {name} leads the night shift. The rota is printed and agreed.
3.hinglish: Night shift {name} lead karenge. Rota chhap gaya aur tay ho gaya.

1.en: {name} leads the night shift. The rota changes twice this week.
1.hinglish: Night shift {name} lead karenge. Is hafte rota do baar badla.

scene.en: You can put one name forward for senior coordinator.
scene.hinglish: Senior coordinator ke liye aap ek naam aage bhej sakte hain.

question.en: Whose name do you put forward?
question.hinglish: Aap kiska naam aage bhejte hain?

text.en: Led parts of the peak from the first week; colleagues often ask for advice.
text.hinglish: Pehle hafte se peak ke hisse lead kiye; colleagues aksar salaah maangte hain.

text.en: Took on the hardest parts of the peak and delivered each one; trusted by the client.
text.hinglish: Peak ke sabse mushkil hisse liye aur har ek poora kiya; client ka bharosa.

2.en: {name}'s name goes forward. The director will decide next month.
2.hinglish: {name} ka naam aage gaya. Director agle mahine faisla karenge.

scene.en: The full dry run of sale day is on Saturday.
scene.hinglish: Sale day ka poora dry run Saturday ko hai.

question.en: Who should lead the dry run? Put them in order.
question.hinglish: Dry run kaun lead karega? Inhe order mein rakhiye.

text.en: Led dry runs for two large launches; both ran clean.
text.hinglish: Do bade launches ke dry run lead kiye; dono bina gadbad ke chale.

text.en: Knows the sale day plan best; has run every practice so far.
text.hinglish: Sale day ka plan sabse achhe se pata; ab tak ki har practice chalayi.

text.en: Will be on the gate in sale week; has not joined the practices.
text.hinglish: Sale week mein gate par duty; practices mein shaamil nahin.

text.en: Has joined one practice as a helper.
text.hinglish: Ek practice mein helper ke roop mein shaamil.

3.en: {name} led the dry run. It finished on time, with a short list of fixes.
3.hinglish: {name} ne dry run lead kiya. Samay par khatam hua, sudhaar ki chhoti list ke saath.

1.en: {name} led the dry run. It ran late, with a long list of fixes.
1.hinglish: {name} ne dry run lead kiya. Der tak chala, sudhaar ki lambi list ke saath.

scene.en: Trucks are unloaded at 5 am on each of 6 days. Nobody wants it.
scene.hinglish: 6 dinon tak har subah 5 baje trucks khaali karne hain. Yeh koi nahin chahta.

question.en: Share the 6 early shifts.

text.en: Lives five minutes from the warehouse.
text.hinglish: Warehouse se paanch minute ki doori par ghar.

text.en: Is an early riser and lives close to the warehouse.
text.hinglish: Subah jaldi uthne ki aadat, aur ghar warehouse ke paas.

text.en: Lives an hour and a half from the warehouse.
text.hinglish: Warehouse se dedh ghante ki doori par ghar.

3.en: {name} took the most early shifts. The trucks are empty by 7.
3.hinglish: Sabse zyada early shifts {name} ke paas gayi. 7 baje tak trucks khaali.

1.en: {name} took the most early shifts, with a long commute. The trucks are empty by 8.
1.hinglish: Lambe safar ke saath sabse zyada early shifts {name} ke paas gayi. 8 baje tak trucks khaali.

even.en: The early shifts were shared evenly. The trucks are empty by 7.30.
even.hinglish: Early shifts barabar baanti gayi. 7.30 tak trucks khaali.

scene.en: Lotus Home's managing director may visit on sale day.
scene.hinglish: Sale day par Lotus Home ke managing director aa sakte hain.

question.en: Who should host the visit? Put them in order.
question.hinglish: Visit kaun host karega? Inhe order mein rakhiye.

text.en: Hosted two client directors at earlier peaks; knows the safety rules for visitors.
text.hinglish: Pehle ke peaks mein do client directors ko host kiya; visitors ke safety niyam pata.

text.en: Ran last year's client tour; the client still mentions it.
text.hinglish: Pichhle saal client tour chalaya; client ab bhi uski baat karta hai.

text.en: Has met client visitors once, as part of a group.
text.hinglish: Ek baar group ke saath client visitors se mile.

text.en: Has not hosted a visit.
text.hinglish: Koi visit host nahin kiya.

3.en: {name} will host the director. The visit route is agreed with safety.
3.hinglish: Director ko {name} host karenge. Visit ka raasta safety team ke saath tay hai.

1.en: {name} will host the director. Safety has asked for a new route.
1.hinglish: Director ko {name} host karenge. Safety team ne naya raasta maanga hai.

scene.en: Sale day opens with a briefing for all three shifts.
scene.hinglish: Sale day teeno shifts ki briefing se shuru hota hai.

question.en: Who should give the sale day briefing? Put them in order.
question.hinglish: Sale day briefing kaun dega? Inhe order mein rakhiye.

text.en: Gave the all hands briefing at the last two peaks; crews listened.
text.hinglish: Pichhle do peaks mein sabki briefing di; crew ne dhyaan se suna.

text.en: Runs the warehouse's weekly safety talks.
text.hinglish: Warehouse ki weekly safety talks chalane ka kaam.

text.en: Has spoken at team meetings, not to all shifts.
text.hinglish: Team meetings mein bole hain, sab shifts ke saamne nahin.

text.en: Prefers not to speak to large groups, but is willing.
text.hinglish: Bade group ke saamne bolna pasand nahin, par taiyaar.

3.en: {name} gave the briefing. The first trucks left early.
3.hinglish: {name} ne briefing di. Pehle trucks jaldi nikle.

1.en: {name} gave the briefing. The first trucks left on time.
1.hinglish: {name} ne briefing di. Pehle trucks samay par nikle.

scene.en: The client wants a final debrief meeting.
scene.hinglish: Client ko aakhri debrief meeting chahiye.

question.en: Who should lead the client debrief?

text.en: Has led the weekly client calls all season.
text.hinglish: Poore season weekly client calls lead ki.

text.en: Owns the final report and its numbers.
text.hinglish: Final report aur uske numbers ki zimmedaari.

2.en: {name} led the debrief. The client asks to work together again next year.
2.hinglish: {name} ne debrief lead kiya. Client agle saal phir saath kaam karna chahta hai.

scene.en: Next month's national logistics expo in Delhi has 6 day passes for the team.
scene.hinglish: Agle mahine Delhi mein national logistics expo ke 6 day passes team ke liye hain.

question.en: Share the 6 expo day passes.

text.en: Will lead next year's peak; the expo is where the suppliers are.
text.hinglish: Agle saal ka peak lead karne ka kaam; expo mein hi suppliers milte hain.

text.en: Is building the warehouse's supplier list for next year.
text.hinglish: Agle saal ke liye warehouse ki supplier list banane ka kaam.

text.en: Has no project planned that needs the expo.
text.hinglish: Aisa koi project nahin jismein expo ki zaroorat ho.

3.en: {name} took the most passes and has booked meetings with five suppliers.
3.hinglish: Sabse zyada passes {name} ko mile; paanch suppliers se meetings tay hain.

1.en: {name} took the most passes, with no meetings booked yet.
1.hinglish: Sabse zyada passes {name} ko mile, par abhi koi meeting tay nahin.

even.en: The passes were shared evenly. Three colleagues will go for two days each.
even.hinglish: Passes barabar baante gaye. Teen colleagues do-do din jaayenge.

scene.en: The company wants a short lessons document from the peak.
scene.hinglish: Company ko peak se seekh ka ek chhota document chahiye.

question.en: Who should write it?

text.en: Kept the season's notes and issue log up to date every day.
text.hinglish: Poore season roz notes aur issue log update kiya.

text.en: Missed most of the planning meetings this season.
text.hinglish: Is season zyaadatar planning meetings mein nahin the.

3.en: {name} wrote the lessons document. The director shares it with other sites.
3.hinglish: {name} ne lessons document likha. Director ne ise doosri sites ke saath share kiya.

1.en: {name} wrote the lessons document. It needs input from others.
1.hinglish: {name} ne lessons document likha. Ismein doosron ki raay chahiye.

scene.en: Some of the peak budget is left over.
scene.hinglish: Peak budget ka kuch hissa bacha hai.

question.en: What do you do with it?

text.en: Return it to the client with the final report
text.hinglish: Final report ke saath client ko lauta dein

after.en: The client thanks you for the clear accounts.
after.hinglish: Saaf hisaab ke liye client ne shukriya kaha.

text.en: Spend it on a team dinner
text.hinglish: Team dinner par kharch karein

after.en: The team enjoys the dinner. The client asks about the bill.
after.hinglish: Team ko dinner pasand aaya. Client ne bill ke baare mein poochha.

text.en: Buy more shelving now
text.hinglish: Abhi aur shelving khareedein

after.en: Sale week is over. The shelving stays in its boxes.
after.hinglish: Sale week khatam ho chuka. Shelving dabbon mein hi padi hai.

scene.en: The team wants to celebrate the peak.
scene.hinglish: Team peak ka jashn manana chahti hai.

question.en: When should the team celebrate?

text.en: Friday lunch, in working hours
text.hinglish: Friday lunch, kaam ke ghanton mein

after.en: Friday lunch is booked. Everyone can come.
after.hinglish: Friday lunch book ho gaya. Sab aa sakte hain.

text.en: Saturday night
text.hinglish: Saturday raat

after.en: Saturday night works for some. Three people cannot come.
after.hinglish: Saturday raat kuch logon ke liye theek hai. Teen log nahin aa sakte.

text.en: Skip the celebration
text.hinglish: Jashn chhod dein

after.en: No celebration. The team chat goes quiet.
after.hinglish: Koi jashn nahin. Team chat shaant ho gayi.

scene.en: The company board wants the peak results presented.
scene.hinglish: Company board peak ke nateeje sunna chahta hai.

question.en: Who should present to the board? Put them in order.
question.hinglish: Board ke saamne kaun present karega? Inhe order mein rakhiye.

text.en: Presented results to the board twice; both were well received.
text.hinglish: Board ko do baar nateeje present kiye; dono baar achha raha.

text.en: Built the peak's final numbers and knows every figure.
text.hinglish: Peak ke final numbers banaye; har aankda pata.

text.en: Has not presented to the board.
text.hinglish: Board ke saamne present nahin kiya.

text.en: Joined halfway through the season.
text.hinglish: Season ke beech mein shaamil hue.

3.en: {name} presented to the board. The board asks the team to run two clients next year.
3.hinglish: {name} ne board ko present kiya. Board ne agle saal do clients sambhalne ko kaha.

1.en: {name} presented to the board. The board asks for the numbers in writing.
1.hinglish: {name} ne board ko present kiya. Board ne numbers likhit mein maange.

premise.en: Peak season is coming. You start from head office, then staff up the warehouse.
premise.hinglish: Peak season aa raha hai. Aap head office se shuru karte hain, phir warehouse ke liye log jodte hain.

premise.en: A week of everyday disputes lands on your desk. Complaints of sexual harassment never go to a team lead: they go to the Internal Committee. These are ordinary workplace disputes.
premise.hinglish: Roz ke jhagdon ka ek hafta aapki table par aata hai. Sexual harassment ki shikayatein kabhi team lead ke paas nahin jaatin: woh Internal Committee ke paas jaati hain. Yeh aam workplace ke jhagde hain.

premise.en: Costs rise and a supplier pulls out. Every rupee and every hour counts.
premise.hinglish: Kharche badhte hain aur ek supplier peeche hat jaata hai. Har rupaya aur har ghanta keemti hai.

premise.en: The company runs its promotion round, and your picks for the big jobs count.
premise.hinglish: Company apna promotion round chalati hai, aur bade kaamon ke liye aapki pasand maayne rakhti hai.

premise.en: Sale week arrives, then the reckoning: who presents, who goes to the expo, what is learnt.
premise.hinglish: Sale week aata hai, phir hisaab: kaun present karega, kaun expo jaayega, kya seekha.

mascots.en: You start at head office. Until you visit the warehouse, you know the team only by the mascots on the team chat.
mascots.hinglish: Aap head office se shuru karte hain. Warehouse jaane tak aap team ko sirf team chat ke mascots se jaante hain.

premise.en: Five episodes on a city newspaper's night desk, from the first edition to election night. PENDING v17
premise.hinglish: Ek shehar ke akhbaar ki night desk par ek season, pehle edition se election ki raat tak. PENDING v17

premise.en: Five episodes running a busy city clinic through the monsoon fever rush. PENDING v17
premise.hinglish: Monsoon bukhaar ke daur mein ek vyast shehri clinic chalane ka season. PENDING v17

pickBody.en: Each season is a short story in five episodes that reads you. Your decisions shape the story, and at the end you see what they say about you. About 12 minutes.
pickBody.hinglish: Har season paanch episodes ki ek chhoti kahani hai jo aapko padhti hai. Aapke decisions kahani banate hain, aur aakhir mein aap dekhte hain ki woh aapke baare mein kya kehte hain. Lagbhag 12 minute.

body.en: When a woman and a man had equally strong notes for a job, you put {group} ahead more often than chance would explain. The pull was small in any one decision; it shows across the season as a whole. That is common: most people's decisions lean one way on some ground, and many never find out. Knowing where yours leaned is the useful part. This reads one season of a made-up warehouse, so treat it as a reading, not a verdict on who you are.
body.hinglish: Jab ek mahila aur ek purush ke kaam ke notes barabar mazboot the, aapne {group} ko itni baar aage rakha jitna sanyog se nahin samjhaya ja sakta. Kisi ek decision mein kheench chhoti thi; yeh poore season mein dikhti hai. Yeh aam baat hai: zyaadatar logon ke decisions kisi aadhaar par ek taraf jhukte hain, aur kai log yeh kabhi nahin jaan paate. Apna jhukaav jaanna hi kaam ki baat hai. Yeh ek kaalpanik warehouse ke ek season ki reading hai, aap kaun hain is par faisla nahin.

body.en: When a woman and a man had equally strong notes for a job, you put each of them ahead about as often as chance would. That is an absence of evidence from about 50 decisions, not a clean bill: a lean too small for one short season to pick up could still be there, and another setting could read differently. Everyone's decisions lean somewhere, so the habits below are worth keeping either way.
body.hinglish: Jab ek mahila aur ek purush ke kaam ke notes barabar mazboot the, aapne dono ko lagbhag utni hi baar aage rakha jitna sanyog se hota. Yeh lagbhag 50 decisions mein saboot ki kami hai, saaf certificate nahin: itna chhota jhukaav ho sakta hai jo ek chhota season na pakad sake, aur kisi aur maahaul mein reading alag ho sakti hai. Har kisi ke decisions kahin na kahin jhukte hain, isliye neeche ki aadatein dono haalat mein kaam ki hain.

body.en: This season does not hold enough decisions of the right kind to read a lean either way. That says nothing about you; it is a limit of one short season.

opening.en: You are the person closest to your own decisions, which makes them the hardest for you to see. This page is a view from outside, read only from the choices you just made. Everyone's decisions lean somewhere, and most people never notice where. Some points below will feel right and some may feel off. When one feels off, ask whether it could still be true.

Har kisi ke decisions kahin na kahin jhukte hain, aur zyaadatar log kabhi notice nahin karte ki kahan. Neeche ki kuch baatein sahi lagengi aur kuch ajeeb. Jo ajeeb lage, us par poochhiye ki kya woh phir bhi sach ho sakti hai.
